newsitem.title: USA: Top senators ask Clinton to name FAA chief quickly.
newsitem.headline: Top senators ask Clinton to name FAA chief quickly.

text.p: Two influential senators urged President Clinton Tuesday to make the nomination of a federal aviation administrator his highest priority.
The post has been vacant since last November when David Hinson resigned after more than three years in office.

Sen. John McCain, the Arizona Republican who is chairman of the Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee, said, "Considering the 1996 aviation accident record, we cannot afford any further erosion in public confidence."
Both passenger deaths and major accidents rose last year.
"We need the most experienced leader to move on many pending FAA reform issues, including safety and security," McCain said.
"After so much talk about safety, it is unconscionable that the administration has not yet nominated an FAA administrator," he said.

The chairman of the committee's panel on aviation, Sen. Slade Gorton, a Washington Republican, said, "It is imperative that the president moves expeditiously on nominating a credible, capable candidate."
He added, "We need strong leadership at the FAA as we work to implement safety and security improvements at our airports. The lack of a nominee hamstrings this process."
